name: MetaScrub — Metadata Audit & Scrub: Find, Remove & Verify Hidden Data in Photos, Office & PDF Files
description:
That photo knows where I live — how do I find, remove and verify the hidden metadata in my photos, documents and PDF files? That document remembers who wrote it.
Before you send a file out, MetaScrub audits it for the data you cannot see: the GPS coordinates in a photo, the camera serial number, the thumbnail of the part you cropped away, the author and revision history in a Word file, the producer data in a PDF. Then it removes that data, writes a cleaned copy, and hands you a report that proves — per file — that the result is zero. Your originals are never touched.
The report is the product. Other metadata cleaners finish with a bare list of "successful" files and no detail about what was actually removed. MetaScrub gives you a per-file triple instead: Found — every hidden item named; Removed — what the scrub took out; Rechecked zero — the cleaned copy is audited again and must read 0 target items remaining. Photo pixels are hash-checked, document and PDF text are hash-checked, and every cleaned file is verified to still open.
What it covers:
- JPEG photos: GPS coordinates, camera Make/Model, serial numbers, software, artist, dates, embedded EXIF thumbnail. Scrubbing strips the whole EXIF block at byte level; pixels are never re-encoded.
- Word / Excel / PowerPoint: author, last editor, revision number, company, custom properties, revision traces (rsid attributes). Scrubbing empties author/editor, resets revision, empties company, removes custom properties, strips rsid attributes; body text untouched.
- PDF: Author, Creator, Producer, Title, Subject, Keywords, XMP metadata. Scrubbing empties info-dictionary fields and XMP metadata; page text untouched.
Measured in our seeded acceptance test (35/35 checks passed): a JPEG planted with GPS, a camera serial number and an embedded thumbnail went from 9 hidden items found to 0 remaining with pixels unchanged; a DOCX planted with author, company and revision traces went from 6 finding groups to 0 with body text unchanged; a PDF planted with Author, Producer and XMP metadata went from 7 items to 0 with page text unchanged. A PDF carrying a signature field was detected and skipped, not scrubbed, with the skip stated explicitly in the report. All 4 original seed files stayed byte-identical (SHA-256 verified).
100% local — your files never leave your computer. Windows 10/11. No account, no subscription.
Honest limits: v1 covers JPEG photos, Office files (docx/xlsx/pptx) and PDFs. PNG, HEIC, TIFF, RAW, video and audio metadata are not scrubbed in this version and are reported as unsupported, never force-converted. Digitally signed PDFs are detected by signature flags and/or a signature-field marker and skipped, never scrubbed, because changing the file would break the signature; detection is marker detection only, not a cryptographic validation. A scrubbed file is not certified or compliant with any law, standard or platform policy, and scrubbing does not remove tracked-change content itself — only the rsid revision-trace attributes. The report lists exactly what was found and removed; read it before sending anything sensitive.
